MG Bhuiyan, Advocate-on-Record------ For the Petitioner.

Abdul Ali Bhuiyan (Md) ------ Petitioner 
Vs.
Jahura Khatun and others ------ Respondents
full_judgment:
Md Tafazzul lslam J: This civil petition for leave to appeal at the instance of the defendant-petitioner arises out of the judgment and order dated 19-1-2002 passed by a Single Bench of the High Court Division in Civil Revision No. 1178 of 1990 discharging the Rule and thereby affirming the judgment and order dated 6-1-1990 passed by learned Subordinate Judge, Netrokona in OC Appeal No. 27 of 1984 affirming those dated 10-4-1979 passed by the learned Munsif, (now Assistant Judge) Netrokona in Partition Suit No. 236 of 1972 decreeing the suit for partition. 

 3. The learned Munsif (now Assistant Judge), 2nd Court, Netrokona, after hearing, decreed the suit in preliminary form. Being aggrieved the defendant No. 8 filed Appeal No. 27 of 1984 which was dismissed. He then filed Civil Revision No. 1178 of 1990 and after hearing the High Court Division discharged the Rule. 

 4. The learned Counsel appearing for the defendant No. 8 petitioner has submitted that the Courts below failed to consider that the defendant No. 8 petitioner is in possession of 87 acres out of suit property which was purchased by him by 3 (three) registered kabalas; the Courts below illegally relied upon the Rafanama entered into between the plaintiff and the defendant No. 1 which was obtained behind the knowledge ofthe defendant No. 8 petitioner; this Rafanama is, in fact, a fraud practised upon the Court by the plaintiff and the defendant No. 1; while decreeing the suit the trial Court did not hear the defendant No. 8 petitioner; partition is to be based on equity, justice and fair play and the Rafanama having been entered into behind the back of the defendant No.8 petitioner, it ought not to have been relied upon by the Courts below and as such the decree is liable to be set aside. 

 5. As it appears the trial Court found that after compromise, by Rafanama the plaintiffs were entitled to get a saham to the extent of 7 annas, which comes to 2.28 acres of land, the defendant No. 1 was entitled to get a saham to the extent of 4 annas 13 gondas 1 kara 1 kranti which comes to 1.52 acres of land, the defendant No. 2 in her 2 annas share in the suit property was entitled to get .65 acres of land but since she gave 0.37 acres of land to defendant No.3 by way of gift, the defendant No.3 thus got 0.76 acres of land in her share but she after taking only 0.20 decimals of land relinquished her claim in respect of the remaining land in favour of the defendant No. 1. Thus both the defendant Nos. 2 and 3 were entitled to saham of 0.85 acres of land and the share of the defendant No. 1 in the suit property came to 2.08 acres of land. However, by registered kabalas Ext A- 1 dated 22-11-1965 the defendant No. 1 sold 67 acres of land to the defendant No. 4(ka) and 4(Uma) and by registered kabalas Ext A-1 dated 3-2-1970 also showed that the defendant sold 0.35 acres of land to the defendant Nos. 5(ka) and 5(kha) and on the basis of the above purchases, the defendant Nos. 4(Ka) 4(Uma) and 5(Ka) 5(Kl)a) were entitled to claim a saham of 1.02 acres of land in the suit land and thereby the defendant No. 1 was left with only 1.06 acres of land. But Ext 'Ka' registered kabala dated 9-3- 1972 shows that the defendant No. 1 sold 0.40 acres of land to defendant No. 6 and Exts 'Kha' and 'Ga', dated 13-3-1972 showed that the defendant No. 1 sold .26 acres and 0.42 acres of land to the defendant 7 and 8 and thus the defendant. No.1 sold in total 1.08 acres of land, though he was left with only 1.06 acres of land. Besides that the defendant No. 1 subsequently executed some other documents in favour of defendant Nos. 8, 10 and 11 though at that time he had no longer any saleable interest in the suit property. Considering the above the trial Court did not give the defendant Nos. 8, 10 and 11 sahams claimed on the basis of subsequent purchases. The lower appellate Court as well as the High Court Division also found that the defendant No. 8 petitioner purchased the suit property in the excess of the shares of his vendor i.e. the defendant No. 1 and further he was very much a party in the partition suit but did not contest the suit by filing any written statement and instead merely prayed for a saham. The Courts below found that the trial Court decreed the suit distributing sahams as per law and the Rafanama, alleged to have been executed between the plaintiff and the defendant No.1, was filed in the partition suit and the defendant No. 8 petitioner, having not raised any objection against the above Rafanama earlier, was not entitled to challenge the same at such belated stage. The Courts below also found that the defendant No.8 petitioner also could not prove his possession to the extent of 0.87 acres as claimed by him.
